pr_comments:
The problem comes from the branch `elif is_float_dtype(data.dtype):` in function `sequence_to_td64ns`.
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/68d9dcab5b543adb3bfe5b83563c61a9b8afae77/pandas/core/arrays/timedeltas.py#L1114
`data` here is a 2D `array([[nan], [ 1.]])`.
But `cast_from_unit_vectorized` only accepts 1D array as input, thus producing the "Buffer has wrong number of dimensions" error (see [issue](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/60064#issuecomment-2428159736)), if I understand correctly the code below:
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/68d9dcab5b543adb3bfe5b83563c61a9b8afae77/pandas/_libs/tslibs/conversion.pyx#L133-L147

I notice that other branches for other dtypes in `sequence_to_td64ns` can work with 2D array data, so come up with this quick fix.
CI should be fixed now. Can you merge main.

> CI should be fixed now. Can you merge main.

Thanks. I merged main and added in whatsnew.

> But cast_from_unit_vectorized only accepts 1D array as input

My preference ideally would be to make cast_from_unit_vectorized correctly handle 2D inputs.  Handling it in _try_cast seems like a fine second-best.

### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame([None, 1], dtype='timedelta64[ns]')
```


### Issue Description

The error message doesn't tell the user what to do differently. Also, it's possible that there shouldn't be an error at all.

### Expected Behavior

I think this should be allowed, in which case the resulting series would look like

```
                          0
0                       NaT
1 0 days 00:00:00.000000001
```

If it's not allowed, the error message should be clearer.
